where: 01_b1_power / 06_b2_power; U101, U601 (CBB011M12GM4T) AC1.1-4 / AC2.1-4 on B1_ACA/B1_ACB, B2_ACA/B2_ACB; sim/out/dab_design/derating_map.csv
finding: The transformer current flows through each module's AC terminals (4 press-fit pins each), and its rms value exceeds the module's 100 A package/press-fit limit inside the published derating map. The design checks only the per-switch-position rms current against the limit (dab_design.py LIM I_pos_rms_max 90 A), but in a full bridge the AC terminal carries the full transformer current: I_AC = sqrt(2) x I_switch.
evidence: CBB011M12GM4T.pdf p7: Fig 20 'Press-Fit Pin Limit' 100 A; Fig 22 'Package limit' 100 A rms output current (inverter application = AC-terminal current); p1 note 2 'current limit imposed by package'. sim/out/dab_design/efficiency_map.csv filtered to feasible points with |P| <= derating_map.csv P_max: 18 (V1, V2, |P|) points, 36 counting both power directions, have IL_rms > 100 A. Worst case 600/750 V +/-60 kW: IL_rms 118.5 A (bridge 1 AC pins), Is_rms 111.9 A (bridge 2). Also 700/650 V 60 kW 118.0 A, 600/800 V 60 kW 114.9 A, 800/650 V 60 kW 113.0 A. Per-switch rms is 83.8 A, below the 90 A check, so the check passes.
recommendation: Add AC-terminal rms <= 100 A (with margin, e.g. 90 A) for both bridges as a constraint in sim/dab_design.py derating(), then regenerate derating_map.csv, the dab_spec stresses and DAB-05. Otherwise take the D-017 option of two modules per bridge. Get Wolfspeed to confirm the per-pin rms rating at 100 kHz (skin effect).

where: 02/03/07/08 gate sheets; every channel's interlock stretcher R203 2.21k / C202 100p / D201 BAT54 / U201 SN74LVC1G17 -> IN- (gdrv.DEADTIME); dab_spec power_stage/dead_time
finding: The drawn hardware forces a minimum dead time that dab_spec says does not exist. dab_spec specifies an adaptive firmware dead time of 50-300 ns (fallback 100 ns) and states 'no hardware dead-time insertion'. Every DAB60 channel, however, uses the gdrv interlock stretcher, which holds the incoming switch off for 104-354 ns at the gates whatever firmware commands. Any firmware value below ~294 ns is overridden, and the effective dead time varies by up to 250 ns between the 8 channels. The ZVS map, the loss model and the derating map all assume the firmware value. The extra body-diode conduction is not in the model. In hard-switched or partial-ZVS edges (TPS at light load), a per-leg spread of up to 250 ns also shifts the switching edges and causes volt-second imbalance.
evidence: hardware/GDRV-HB/outputs/GDRV-HB_design_check.txt: 'dead time (stretch 2.21k/100p, firmware DT = 0): 104-354 ns at the gates ... a firmware DT >= 294 ns is never extended'. Netlist: B1_PWM_L1 -> R203 2.21k -> DTS_B1H1 (C202 100p, D201) -> U201 -> R204 -> U203 pin 11 IN-, and the same on all 8 channels. dab_spec.json power_stage.dead_time: min 50, max 300, fallback 100 ns, 'no hardware dead-time insertion'. CBB011M12GM4T.pdf p3: VSD 5.4-5.8 V at 100 A versus ~2.3 V channel drop. Calculation: about 250 ns extra diode conduction x 4 edges x 100 kHz x (5.5-2.3) V x 130 A = ~40 W per bridge at heavy load, not in the loss model. dab_spec flux_balance: 25 A DC per 5 ns of open-loop edge skew. CRD UG Table 11: 200 ns fixed dead time from firmware.
recommendation: Decide which element owns the dead time. Either shrink the stretcher to a pure shoot-through interlock (worst-case maximum below the 50 ns firmware minimum, e.g. ~470 R / 100 p, rechecked against t_off 75 ns + driver skew), or put the hardware dead-time window into dab_spec and rerun the loss, ZVS, derating and flux-balance analyses with it. In both cases the dead-time spread should be smaller than the flux-balance loop can absorb.

where: 04_b1_if / 09_b2_if (U404-U408 TRIP_N/LATCH/EN_DRV/RUN), 05_b1_sense / 10_b2_sense (U506 TLV3502 OC window, U507 ISO7720F), 16_io (OV comparators); dab_spec protection
finding: The firmware-independent trips switch off with the fast gate path, at currents and voltages outside the module's switching SOA. The local transformer-OC window (+/-210 A, band 200-220 A, 0.78 us to the gate) and the port OV trip both act through RUN/EN_DRV, so every switch does a normal turn-off through Roff = 0.27 ohm. The UCC21710 400 mA soft turn-off is used only by its own DESAT. CBB011M12GM4T switching SOA (Fig 19, 24 nH): 180 A chip ceiling at any voltage, falling to about 100 A at 1000 V. The OC trip level alone is above that ceiling. During the 0.78 us response the current can still rise by (V1 + n V2)/L = 1775 V / 6.5 uH = 273 A/us, so turn-off can reach about 420 A. dab_spec's voltage-dependent OC limit sits in the CTRL CMPSS on AN1. AN1 passes through the AMC3330 with 1.6-2.6 us signal delay, so it acts after the local trip and cannot keep turn-off inside the SOA. The OV hardware trip turns off up to 113 A at 1029 V, where Fig 19 allows only about 75-85 A, as dab_spec local_ov_board itself notes.
evidence: CBB011M12GM4T.pdf p7 Fig 19 (chip 180 A; module turn-off 0 ohm from 180 A at 840 V to 0 A at 1200 V). UCC21710.pdf p1/p9: ISTO 250-570 mA soft turn-off only on an OC-pin fault; p3 RST/EN low = 'regular turn-off'. AMC3330.pdf p9 (SBASA34B): VIN-to-VOUT delay 1.6-2.1 us (50-50 %), 2.2-2.6 us (50-90 %). DAB60_design_check.txt: OC trips +211/-210 A, 0.78 us to the gate; port 1 OV peak 1029 V. dab_spec worst_case_stresses.I_turn_off_max_bridge1 177 A (normal operation already at the 180 A ceiling); verdict_950V: 113 A allowed at 950 V. No avalanche rating is published for the module.
recommendation: Route the fast local OC trip into the drivers' soft turn-off. The OC comparator sits on HV1 DC-, so it can pull the OC pins of the two low-side drivers (same reference) through a diode-OR and let the high side follow on FLT/RUN. Alternatively use a two-step turn-off (larger Roff on a fault). Make the local OC level voltage-dependent in hardware, with the port OV comparator data as input, or lower it, and include the response-time ramp in the SOA check (dab_design.py). Update dab_spec: the CMPSS-on-AN1 path cannot be the voltage-dependent protection because of the AMC3330 delay.

where: 04_b1_if / 09_b2_if: TRIP_N, LATCH_OK, EN_DRV, RUN and DRV_FLT_N are per bridge; only OV_OK (16_io) is shared. CTRL pin plan (gen/ctrl_c2000.py ~l.427: 'each ePWM ORs its own TRIP with TRIP9')
finding: No hardware links the two bridges' trips. A DESAT, local OC, DC-flux, +24V UV or driver UVLO/bias-PG fault on one bridge gates only that bridge's 4 PWMs. A dead bias supply, a tripped CELL eFuse or an unplugged/unpowered bridge board does the same. The other bridge keeps switching until the CTRL acts. The CTRL can act only through firmware-configured X-BAR routing, and the documented routing does not cross-trip: C1_FAULT -> TRIP4 for ePWM1-2, C2_FAULT -> TRIP5 for ePWM5-6, and Cn_DRV_EN = CHB_OK & EN_MCU & own RDY. Meanwhile the stopped bridge's switch nodes are driven by the transformer through its body diodes (63 A DC rating, VSD 5.4-5.8 V). If the stopped bridge has no bias (cable out, bias dead), its gates are held only by 10 k and the UCC21710 unpowered active pull-down (1.5-2.5 V), with no Miller clamp, no negative bias and no DESAT. Commutation dv/dt from the running bridge can then turn it on into a shoot-through. ECO-05/task: every fault must turn all 8 gates off without firmware.
evidence: Netlist: U404/U405/U406/U408 (B1) use only B1_* nets plus OV_OK, and U904-U908 (B2) likewise. CTRL: gen/ctrl_c2000.py lines 346-356, 427-439 (per-cell TRIPn, Cn_DRV_EN = CHB_OK AND Cn_EN_MCU AND Cn_RDY). UCC21710.pdf p9: VOUTPD 1.5-2.5 V with VDD open. CBB011M12GM4T.pdf p2: VGS(th) min 1.8 V (25 C), 2.0 V typ at 175 C; p3 ISD,BD 63 A. CRD UG p38: 'without proper firmware implementation, only the tripped gate driver(s) will turn off'.
recommendation: Cross-couple the two bridge logic blocks on DAB60. Both are PELV and GND-referenced, so it is cheap: for example AND each bridge's RUN and EN_DRV with the other bridge's H_OK/TRIP_N, or form a common TRIP_N/LATCH. Then any trip, RDY loss or missing +24V on either bridge stops both. A missing board must read as a trip, so the signal needs a pull-down to 'fault' on the receiving side. Also state in the CTRL pin plan that for DAB the C1/C2 FAULT and RDY events trip ePWM1-2 and 5-6 together.

where: 02/03/07/08 gate sheets: DESAT networks R215 3.74k / R216 24.9k / R217 1.87k / C219 100p (gdrv.DESAT) on all 8 channels; dab_spec gate_drive.desat
finding: The DESAT response margin rests on an optimistic withstand time, and our blanking is longer than in Wolfspeed's own design for this module. dab_spec takes t_sc = 2.0 us 'at <= 950 V, VGS 15 V' and reports the 1.32 us worst-case response as 66 % of it. The only source is a Wolfspeed marketing brief: 'the automotive die EM4E120-025D100 based on Gen 4 technology can tolerate up to a two-microsecond (2.3 us) short circuit'. That is a best case, for a different die, with no voltage or Tj stated. Our port 1 runs at 950-1000 V and up to Tj 136 C (more in the pessimistic case). SC withstand time falls with both bus voltage and starting Tj, so the real margin is unknown and could be negative. Wolfspeed's CRD60DD12N-GMB DESAT uses R38 220 ohm / C21 56 pF (tau about 12 ns), i.e. effectively no RC blanking: it relies on the driver's internal 95-180 ns OC filter. Ours adds 178-367 ns. (The CRD network has its own defect: open-circuit OC = 15 V x 220/4620 = 0.714 V, below VOCTH max 0.77 V, so it may never trip. Do not copy it.)
evidence: docs/datasheets/power-semiconductors/Wolfspeed_Designed_to_Last_Even_in_the_Harshest_Environments.pdf p8 (application brief, 'NOT A DATASHEET' per SOURCES.csv): EM4E120-025D100 'up to a two-microsecond (2.3us)'. CBB011M12GM4T.pdf: no tSC given anywhere. CRD60DD12N-GMB-CONTROL V2.0 schematic p3 (PRIMARY GATE 2): R34 2.2k, R36 2.2k, R38 220R, C21 56 pF, D14 BAT42W, 2 x US3M-13. UCC21710.pdf p9: tOCFIL 95-180 ns, tOCOFF 150-400 ns, VOCTH 0.63-0.77 V. DAB60_design_check.txt: blanking 178-367 ns, worst-case response 1.319 us.
recommendation: Reduce Cblk to about 47-56 pF, which gives roughly 85-185 ns of RC blanking and still covers the hard-switched turn-on fall time; recheck with the gdrv desat_numbers() window. That cuts the worst-case response to about 1.1 us. Ask Wolfspeed for CBB011M12GM4T short-circuit data at 1000 V / Tj 150 C / VGS 15 V. Until then do not quote a margin: mark t_sc as unknown in dab_spec and list an SC test before any operation above 800 V.

where: 02_b1_gatea / 07_b2_gatea (module NTC T1/T2 -> L1 driver AIN/APWM -> B1_AN2 / B2_AN2), 05/10 sense AN3 (transformer winding NTC, coolant probe); D-017
finding: No hardware over-temperature trip on the board. The module NTCs (AIN -> APWM -> AN2, 10 ms filter) and the transformer winding NTC (AN3) reach only the CTRL ADC, i.e. firmware. The only firmware-independent thermal trip is the coolant loop (flow switch + 77 C cold-plate thermostat via SYS-IO-AUX J801). With Rth,hf = 0.045 K/W, a loss excursion of a few hundred watts in one module (lost ZVS, wrong TPS LUT entry, the D-017 pessimistic case) raises the cold plate by only ~10-15 K and will not open it, while Tj climbs. D-017's statement that 'the module NTC trip protects the hardware' is therefore firmware-dependent. The substrate NTC also lags Tj by Rth,JH x P (0.429 K/W x 200-300 W = 85-130 K in the pessimistic case of 196 C Tj). Every NTC chain also fails 'cold': an open module NTC gives AIN 4.35 V (= colder than -40 C), and an open transformer or coolant NTC on AN3 reads ~0 V (= coldest).
evidence: Netlist: B1_NTC -> U206 (L1 driver) pin 1 AIN; APWM -> 10k/100k/1u -> OPA2388 -> B1_AN2_P -> J401 pin 33. No comparator on AN2 or AN3 feeds TRIP_N. dab_spec protection.module_ntc_trip_C 110 (firmware). DECISIONS D-017. CBB011M12GM4T.pdf p2 Rth,JH 0.429 K/W. dab_spec thermal Rth_hf_K_W 0.045; pessimistic.modules Tj_max_C 196. gdrv design check: 'AIN 4.35 V open, 3.62 V at 25 C'; AN3 = 3.0 V x Rb/(R_NTC + 100 + Rb), so an open NTC gives 0 V.
recommendation: Add a hardware comparator on AN2 of each bridge (APWM duty is ratiometric to 3V3_B; compare the filtered AN2 against a 3V3-derived threshold) into TRIP_N, plus a comparator on the transformer NTC (AN3 bridge 1) and on the transformer inductor NTC if fitted. Set the NTC trip from a modelled NTC-to-Tj offset at the worst loss point, not 110 C on the substrate. Correct the D-017 wording.

where: 01_b1_power / 06_b2_power: C116-C125, C616-C625 (10 x 47 nF C0G >= 1.5 kV, RFQ) and R101-R112 / R601-R612 (13.6 ohm 3 W 2512, RFQ); dab_spec dc_link_snubber_hf
finding: The terminal network's ratings were checked only for the RC resistors, and that check rests on the HF capacitors. The resistor power (1.21 W per 3 W part) assumes the 10 HF MLCCs absorb most of the bus ring-down: with them modelled as ESR 10 mohm / ESL 1 nH each (assumed), the resistors take ~1.2 W; without them, 10.8 W per 3 W resistor. Nobody checked what this does to the HF MLCCs themselves. In the designer's own ngspice deck at the ioffmax point, the 10 x 47 nF carry 143 A rms (14.3 A rms and 40 A peak per capacitor) and dissipate 20.5 W, i.e. 2.05 W per 2220/1812 MLCC. At v1max the figures are 7.5 A rms and 0.57 W per capacitor. A 2220 MLCC cannot shed 2 W. The RFQ text gives only C, dielectric, voltage and case, with no ripple-current or dissipation requirement and no candidate part.
evidence: Scratch run of the designer's deck sim/spice/dab_snub_ioffmax_rc_hf.cir (circuit unchanged; measurements of Rhf1, Lhf1 and Rsn1 added): HF-cap ESR power 20.5 W, I_rms 143 A, I_pk 399 A for the 10 caps together. The RC resistors take 14.5 W in the deck's CRD 6-branch model, i.e. 2.42 W per CRD resistor = 1.21 W per resistor in our 12-branch network. v1max deck: 5.7 W, 75 A rms. dab_spec P_ring_max_W_per_bridge 28.6 W map-wide; snubber_study.csv gives 106 W analytic ring-down at the ioffmax point. The deck's film bank (Ck1) has no ESR, so the split between elements is a model result, not a bound. The CRD fits 47 nF 1 kV film capacitors here (KEMET LDEQ, 5040 case), 10 + 13 per side.
recommendation: Specify the HF capacitor by ripple current and dissipation as well as C/V (>= 15 A rms at MHz, temperature rise), or change the concept: film snubber caps such as KEMET LDE/KC-LINK class rated at >= 1.5 kV, or more and smaller parts. Rerun the deck with realistic bank ESR, HF-cap ESR/ESL and copper, and check every element of the terminal network against its rating at all four study points. Give the RFQ the resulting current and power.

where: 06_b2_power C601-C603 (C4AQQEW5650A3BJ, 1100 V class); 01_b1_power C101-C103; dab_spec capacitor_banks
finding: The hot-spot estimate that sets the bank voltage margin is optimistic. sim/dab_design.py takes 60 C local air (the maximum PV-20 ambient, with no internal rise) and the 10 kHz ESR, but the bank ripple is at 200 kHz and above. That is above the capacitor's own resonance: 45 uF / 65 uF with 19 nH ESL resonate at 172 / 143 kHz. Port 2's 1100 V-class part is allowed only 950 V at THS 81 C and 900 V at 85 C, against 900 V operating and a 950 V OV trip. So port 2 keeps its rating only while the hot spot stays at or below about 81 C, which leaves about 12 K for the internal air rise plus any ESR increase.
evidence: C4AQ.pdf p6 operative derating (1100 V: VOP85 900 V), p14 table row C4AQQEW5650A3BJ (ESR 2.6 mohm at 10 kHz, ESL 19 nH, Rth 7 K/W, Irms note: 30 K rise). sim/dab_design.py l.1165 't_hot = 60.0 + icap^2 * esr * rth'. dab_spec port2 hot spot 68.5 C, V_allowed 1100 V.
recommendation: Use the 1300 V-class part on port 2 as well (C4AQUEW5450A3BJ, 4-5 per bank for C), or get KEMET's ESR at 200 kHz-1 MHz and define the internal air temperature of the module (it is not in REQUIREMENTS for DAB). Then re-run the hot-spot check at the real ambient.

where: 12_portA_power / 14_portB_power (port.port(): F1201-F1402 HP10NH1GPV160 gPV fuses, FV1201/FV1401 DEHNguard M YPV SCI 1000 FM)
finding: Both DAB ports face a battery rack or a stiff PCS DC bus, but the port blocks are PV-rated. The fuses are gPV class (IEC 60269-6, PV string fault currents) and the SPDs are PV types (YPV SCI, rated for PV short-circuit current only). Battery and DC-bus faults have much higher prospective current and a longer L/R, which needs gBat-class fuses and a battery-rated DC SPD. port_spec itself leaves port B's SPD OPEN (PA-06). The port agent is adding a 'battery' source type now; recorded once here so DAB60 picks it up for both ports.
evidence: sim/out/port_design/port_spec.json spd.port_B: 'OPEN (PA-06): needs a battery-rated DC SPD'; variants.135.fuse_mpn HP10NH1GPV160; dab_spec parallel_branch_interface per_branch_hardware uses the same 135 A variant. BOM items 15, 16.
recommendation: When port.py gains the battery source type, build DAB60 port A and port B with it (gBat fuse, battery-rated SPD), and redo the hold-closed and contactor coordination of D-019 with the battery or DC-bus prospective current and time constant, for N paralleled branches (DAB-09).

where: 04_b1_if / 09_b2_if: B1_RDY_L, B2_RDY_L -> U405/U905 gate 2 (LR_OK) only, not TRIP_N / U407 PRE
finding: A driver UVLO or bias power-good fault is not latched on the board. RDY_L drops LR_OK, then EN_DRV and RUN, but it does not set the LVC1G74 latch. When RDY returns (after the UCC21710's 0.55-1 ms hold), EN_DRV rises again and the bridge resumes switching with no EN cycle from the CTRL. That rising RST/EN edge (after > 1 us low) also clears any latched DESAT fault in the drivers. The CTRL re-enables its PWM line drivers automatically as well (Cn_DRV_EN contains Cn_RDY). Only a firmware-configured one-shot trip zone holds the bridge off. The task rule is that every fault latches.
evidence: Netlist: TRIP_N = U404/U405 AND of OCH/OCL/DCH/DCL/OV/UV only; LR_OK = LATCH_OK & RDY_L. UCC21710.pdf p3 (RST/EN rising edge resets FLT after > 1000 ns low), p9 tRDYHLD 0.55-1 ms. DAB60_design_check 'Logic' line: RDY_L appears in FLT, EN_DRV and RUN but not in the latch. gen/ctrl_c2000.py l.857.
recommendation: Feed RDY_L into the latch (e.g. TRIP_N = ... & RDY_L, or a second PRE term), so a bias or UVLO dip needs an explicit EN cycle. Keep RDY_DRV to the CTRL as it is.

where: 16_io: U1603 OPA2388 (both OV comparators), U1602 REF3020E, U1604 SN74LVC1G08 -> OV_OK (one net into U404 and U904); inputs VA_P/VA_N (U1301), VB_P/VB_N (U1501)
finding: The hardware OV trip and the firmware OV (960/920 V) read the same port AMC3330 and 6 M / 4.99 k divider. One silent drift or failure in that chain disables both: a divider element going high-ohmic, or an AMC3330 gain or offset error. The OV trip is the only protection of the 1100 V-class port 2 bank and of the module's 1200 V when a battery contactor opens at load. The hardware OV is also a single chain for both bridges: one OPA2388 and one LVC1G08 output (U1604) drive OV_OK into both TRIP_N gates, so one stuck-high output removes the hardware OV of both ports. There is no independent OV sensor. The only coverage is a firmware plausibility check of VA against VAX (and VB against VBX) while the contactor is closed.
evidence: Netlist: OV1_X/OV1_Y dividers are fed from VA_P/VA_N, the same nets that go to the PORT connector for the CTRL ADC. dab_design_check: 'firmware trip ... (same AMC3330)'. port_spec divider: 6 x 1 M TNPV1206.
recommendation: Either derive the hardware OV from VAX/VBX (the terminal-side AMC3330, which is a different part) so that hardware and firmware use independent sensors, or document the VA/VAX plausibility check as a required firmware diagnostic with a time limit in the safety concept.

finding: In the port-short case the film bank carries 5.3 kA (port 1) and 5.9 kA (port 2) per capacitor. KEMET allows 1.5 x Ipkr non-repetitive, i.e. 894 A and 1076 A, and dV/dt of 13 / 11 V/us against about 117 / 91 V/us in this event. The fault analysis covers the module body diodes, the DD600N16K and the fuse, but not the bank, so after a terminal short the bank is outside its rating.
evidence: C4AQ.pdf p5 ('Peak Non-Repetitive Current 1.5 x IPKR for maximum 1,000 times in a lifetime'), p14 table: C4AQUEW5450A3BJ dV/dt 13 V/us, Ipkr 596 A; C4AQQEW5650A3BJ 11 V/us, 717 A. dab_spec dc_link_reverse_clamp port1 I_pk 15.77 kA, port2 17.84 kA, 3 capacitors each.
recommendation: State in the fault analysis and the service documentation that the bank is replaced or inspected after a terminal short, or ask KEMET for a single-surge rating at about 6 kA / 0.5 ms.

where: BOM items 147 (1.6M 0.1 % 0603, R in the DC-flux difference amps of both bridges), 179 (402k 0.1 % 0603, readback), 108 (13.6R 3 W 2512 RFQ)
finding: Some lines marked GENERIC/RFQ are not jellybean parts. 0.1 % thin film in 0603 stops at 332 k in the Vishay series on file, so 1.6 M and 402 k at 0.1 % 0603 are at best single-source. 13.6 ohm is not in E96 or E192 (13.7 / 13.5), and a 3 W rating in a 2512 thick-film case is not a standard catalog rating. The RFQ needs a value and a pulse/energy rating a vendor can quote. The CRD uses standard 6.8 ohm 1.5 W 2512 parts here.
evidence: docs/datasheets/passives-capacitors/TNPW-e3.pdf p1: TNPW0603 1 ohm to 332 kohm (TNPW1206 to 2 Mohm). dab_spec dc_link_snubber_hf note: 'nearest standard parts 13.7 ohm (E96)'.
recommendation: Move the 1.6 M and 402 k to 1206 (TNPW1206, as in the docs) or rescale the DC-flux amplifier (e.g. 10 k / 160 k with 6.2 nF). Write the snubber RFQ as 13.7 ohm 1 %, >= 2 W continuous with the board thermal path, and state the pulse energy per edge from the ngspice deck.

where: 11_magnetics L1101 (series L, CUSTOM); module BOM 'cold plate' (CUSTOM); T1101 description
finding: Two CUSTOM specs are not complete enough to quote safely. (1) The series inductor text has L, current, saturation and loss but no insulation requirement. Its winding sits at the bridge-1 switch-node potential (0-1000 V, 57 V/ns at 100 kHz) and it is cold-plate mounted (PE), so it needs basic insulation to PE for the port-1 working voltage plus a partial-discharge requirement, like the CM choke line. (2) The cold plate is one line: '0.045 K/W per switch position at 9 L/min'. It lacks the total heat load (~1.0-2.4 kW incl. the pessimistic case), coolant (glycol mix, 50 C inlet), pressure rating and drop, module flatness/finish for the pre-applied TIM, the mounting pattern for the transformer, inductor and DD600N16K, and the flow order dab_spec requires (port-2 module first). Wolfspeed's CRD cold-plate drawings are on file and could be referenced.
evidence: bom/DAB-D60_module_BOM.csv items 1 (inductor) and 11 (cold plate); item 4 CM choke has 'winding-core basic insulation'. dab_spec thermal.flow_order; pessimistic.modules coolant_heat_W_max_60kW 2447 W. docs/reference-designs/wolfspeed/crd60dd12n-gmb/design-files/CRD60DD12N-GMB Coldplate (T1.0, B1.2)/.
recommendation: Add the insulation class and working voltage to PE, the PD level and the dv/dt to the series-inductor RFQ (and the core/cold-plate insulation of the transformer windings). Write a cold-plate specification with heat-load map, coolant, pressure, flatness and mounting, starting from the CRD drawing.

where: 04_b1_if / 09_b2_if: U404/U904 (OC_OK, DC_OK, I_OK, IV_OK), U405/U905 (TRIP_N, LR_OK, EN_DRV), U407/U907 (LATCH_OK); 16_io U1603/U1604 (OV_OK)
finding: The local trip chain is single-channel and has no proof test, so a latent single fault removes it and can hide the fault report. A stuck-at-1 analysis of the drawn netlist gives the following. A stuck-high TRIP_N, IV_OK or LATCH_OK disables the OC, DC-flux, OV and +24V UV trips of that bridge. A stuck-high LR_OK or EN_DRV also disables the driver-UVLO action. A stuck-high I_OK or OC_OK disables the OC trip. For TRIP_N, IV_OK, I_OK and OC_OK the fault is also not reported, because FLT_OK is derived from the same TRIP_N. A stuck-high U1603 or U1604 output removes the hardware OV of both bridges. What remains is DESAT, which is independent, so a real short is still turned off, plus the CTRL's firmware-configured CMPSS/trip-zone paths (port OV backup on TRIP9; AN1 window, 2 us late). Nothing tests these gates in service. The PV-PORT hold logic has a proof test; the bridge trip logic does not.
evidence: Scratch evaluation of the netlist (gates of U404-U408 forced stuck-at-1 one at a time, each fault input taken low): TRIP_N/LATCH_OK stuck -> OCH, DCH, OV, UV not stopping the gates; LR_OK/EN_DRV stuck -> plus RDY_L; IV_OK -> OCH, DCH, OV; I_OK -> OCH, DCH; OC_OK -> OCH.
